title: More Features Are Not More Evidence: Limits of Training-Free Human Activity Recognition with Jev
abstract: arXiv:2609.36154v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: General-purpose models promise sensor-based decisions without training a task-specific classifier, which could reduce the dependence of Human Activity Recognition (HAR) on labeled data. Yet it remains unclear whether such models can directly interpret deterministic descriptions of physical sensor signals well enough to replace or complement trained HAR models. We study this question using Jev, a fixed general-purpose probabilistic decision model, on 1,800 class-balanced accelerometer windows from WISDM, UCI341, and PAMAP2. Jev receives no labeled examples, retrieval context, or HAR-specific parameter updates. We evaluate three deterministic sensor representations and compare 5,400 Jev decisions with a generative baseline and three supervised HAR models. translated_title: 更多特征并非更多证据：基于Jev的无训练人类活动识别的局限性
translated_abstract: 通用模型有望在不训练任务特定分类器的情况下实现基于传感器的决策，从而减少人类活动识别（HAR）对标注数据的依赖。然而，此类模型能否直接充分解读物理传感器信号的确定性描述，进而替代或补充经过训练的HAR模型，目前仍不明确。我们使用Jev——一个固定的通用概率决策模型——对来自WISDM、UCI341和PAMAP2数据集的1,800个类别均衡的加速度计窗口开展研究。Jev未接收任何标注样本、检索上下文或针对HAR的参数更新。我们评估了三种确定性传感器表示，并将5,400次Jev决策与一个生成式基线以及三个监督式HAR模型进行比较。结果显示，Jev的表现远低于监督式识别方法，其最强的传感器表示在三个数据集上的宏观F1分别仅为0.038、0.118和0.089，而监督式模型则达到0.686至0.907。
tldr: 研究通过在三个公开数据集上的系统实验表明，无需训练的通用概率决策模型Jev在人类活动识别任务上远逊于监督式模型，证明更多的传感器特征描述并不能转化为更有效的识别证据。
